name: James Butler
role: Medora carpenter; later railroading in the Black Hills
bio: James Butler married Julia Butler in Medora's Catholic church at the end of December 1884, with Father Martin officiating, and the couple set up house at the Cantonment. In March 1885 he was building the skating rink, with E. G. Paddock's livery stable to follow, arranged to make new pews for the church, and welcomed a son at Thanksgiving 1885; by July 1886 he was railroading in the Black Hills, and Mrs. Butler left to join him.

mentions: BUTLER—BUTLER—December 30, 188[1?], in the Catholic church at Medora, Dakota, by the Rev. Father Martin, James Butler and Julia Butler, both of Medora.  A change from the singl…

Father Martin came Monday evening, and Tuesday morning made James and Julia Butler one. He says that the library books will be here Tuesday or Wednesday. They will be in charge of John O'Sullivan. Arrangements for drawing them are not made, but some si…
Mr. and Mrs. J. H. Butler have started housekeeping at the Cantonment.
Jim. Butler will begin the erection of E. G. Paddock's livery stable as soon as he finishes the skating rink.
Rev. Father Martin came up night before last and celebrated mass this morning.
Father Martin has made arrangements with Jim Butler, by which new pews will soon adorn the Catholic church.

Congrtulations are in order and for the last week have been showered on James Butler and wife. Their Thanksgiving present was in the shape of a thirteen-and-a-half pound baby boy. Mother and son are doing finely.
Mrs. James Butler will leave for the Black Hills in a few days to join her husband who is railroading there.
